title: Brazil2026ElectionFilter is registered unconditionally with no feature-switch gate
claim: Brazil2026ElectionFilter exists, is registered in the pre-scoring filter list of PhoenixCandidatePipeline, and does not override the Filter trait's enable() method, so it inherits the trait default of unconditional true -- unlike other request-path features (e.g. BidirectionalFollowHydrator) that are explicitly gated by a named param.
runtime_caveats: No checked-in evidence bounds who is in BRAZIL_2026_ELECTION_USER_IDS beyond the hardcoded static set; the list's currency/accuracy relative to the actual Electoral Court reporting is not verifiable from source.
Whether this code path is actually invoked for real Brazilian users in production, and under what request-routing/geo conditions, is not established by the checked-in filter alone.
notes: Legal/political special case per lens L06. S00 records only that the code exists, is registered, and has no local runtime gate; it does not and cannot establish production activation, and does not assert any legal conclusion.

title: README's illustrative '468x' weight example exactly matches current checked-in ReportWeight/FavoriteWeight ratio
claim: The README's misconception explanation uses the specific number '468' as an example of a report-to-like weight ratio; the current checked-in constants are ReportWeight = -234.0 and FavoriteWeight = 0.5, whose magnitude ratio is exactly 468 (234 / 0.5 = 468).
runtime_caveats: This is the checked-in default only; the actual runtime value used for any given production request could differ via feature-switch override.
notes: Worth flagging because it shows the doc's example number is not an arbitrary round figure chosen purely for pedagogy -- it is traceable to a specific, currently-checked-in pair of constants. This strengthens (but does not by itself prove) the doc's implicit claim that the example reflects real production-relevant weight values.

title: Checked-in BidirectionalFollowReplyWeightBoost default reflects the doc's July 24 value (15.0), not its July 13 value (20.0)
claim: docs/BIDIRECTIONAL_BOOST_CHANGE.md shows two sequential diffs to BidirectionalFollowReplyWeightBoost's default: 20.0 (introduced July 13) then changed to 15.0 (July 24). The current snapshot's param.rs contains only the end state, 15.0.
runtime_caveats: This confirms the checked-in DEFAULT only. It does not by itself prove that 15.0 is the value actually served to any given production user, since xai_feature_switches allows runtime override of param defaults.
notes: This is the clearest example in S00's scope of the README's claim (checked-in defaults are periodically synced to reflect production values) being consistent with an observable, checked-in artifact, for one specific parameter. It does not verify the cron-sync mechanism itself (see S00-F013), only that the end value in the snapshot matches the doc's narrated end state.

title: BidirectionalFollowDwellWeightBoost checked-in default remains 0.0 (no-op), consistent with 'not shipped more broadly' claim
claim: BidirectionalFollowDwellWeightBoost's checked-in default is 0.0, and dwell_weight_for() only applies the boost when the value is nonzero, so the dwell-boost code path is present but inert at the current checked-in default.
runtime_caveats: A zero checked-in default does not preclude a nonzero runtime override being active for some experiment population; the snapshot cannot see feature-switch state.
notes: Reachability chain (L03): DECLARED, EXPORTED, CONSTRUCTED, CALLED all proven; ENABLE CONDITION (nonzero boost) is checked-in FALSE by default, so the code is currently a documented no-op absent runtime override.

title: Current bidirectional_follow_hydrator.rs has materially diverged from the diff shown in docs/BIDIRECTIONAL_BOOST_CHANGE.md
claim: The doc's July 13 diff shows BidirectionalFollowHydrator gating solely on EnableBidirectionalFollowHydration and checking mutual-follow status only for authors the viewer already follows. The current checked-in file additionally: (a) imports and reads a second param, EnableAllAuthorFollowHydration (checked-in default true), which -- when true -- expands the author-check set to ALL candidate authors rather than only followed ones; (b) adds a `!query.has_cached_posts` condition to enable(), so the hydrator is skipped when the query already has cached posts; (c) introduces and populates a new candidate field, author_follows_viewer, that is not mentioned in the doc or the README.
runtime_caveats: The doc explicitly frames itself as a historical, illustrative example ('here's what you might've seen'), dated to a July 2026 diff, while the snapshot is captured 2026-08-14/15; some evolution beyond the shown diff is therefore expected and not itself a defect.
The extent to which EnableAllAuthorFollowHydration's true default is itself a later runtime-configured value vs. a fixed checked-in decision is not established beyond the param.rs text.
notes: See also S00-F007. A reader relying on the docs/BIDIRECTIONAL_BOOST_CHANGE.md diff as a literal, current description of the hydrator's behavior would be materially misled about what the file currently does. This is documentation drift (lens L18), not a code defect.

title: author_follows_viewer is traced end-to-end into the Phoenix prediction request sent via PhoenixScorer's dispatch; trained-model consumption remains a separate, unproven question
claim: The candidate field author_follows_viewer (populated by BidirectionalFollowHydrator when EnableAllAuthorFollowHydration is true) is read by PostCandidate::as_tweet_info (CandidateHelpers trait impl) and mapped into xai_recsys_proto::AuthorInfo.is_following_user, a field of the TweetInfo message built for every candidate. home-mixer/util/phoenix_request.rs's build_tweet_infos() calls as_tweet_info() for each candidate and build_prediction_request() assembles the resulting TweetInfo list into a PredictNextActionsRequest. home-mixer/scorers/phoenix_scorer.rs's PhoenixScorer::score() calls build_prediction_request() and then passes the request to self.dispatch.predict_with_fallback(query, cluster, request) -- PredictionDispatch is the same dispatch abstraction PhoenixScorer holds as its `dispatch` field. This proves DIRECTLY, end-to-end in checked-in source, that the signal is placed into the candidate TweetInfo included in the Phoenix prediction request and that request is sent through PhoenixScorer's prediction dispatch. It does NOT by itself prove that the trained Phoenix model's learned parameters give this field any material influence on output predictions -- PredictionDispatch and predict_with_fallback are defined in the external xai_candidate_pipeline::component_library::egress module (re-exported, not implemented, in home-mixer/util/egress.rs), which is not part of this published snapshot, so the actual network dispatch and any model-serving-side handling are unverifiable from source. Separately, phoenix/crates/common/xai-recsys/src/util.rs -- which IS part of this snapshot -- shows a candidate_is_author_following feature array (InputBuffer::new_with_candidates) and a history_is_author_following feature array (InputBuffer::compute_for_item) both being populated by reading exactly this AuthorInfo.is_following_user field, which is STRONG_INFERENCE (not yet DIRECT proof of trained-model behavioral impact) that the field is intended as, and structurally wired as, a model input feature on the Phoenix serving side.

source_evidence.symbol_or_section: How It Works - Scoring and Ranking

verification_evidence.symbol_or_section: impl CandidateHelpers for PostCandidate, fn as_tweet_info body
pub fn build_tweet_infos -- maps every candidate through candidate_to_tweet_info
pub fn build_prediction_request -- assembles PredictNextActionsRequest from build_tweet_infos() output
async fn score -- let request = build_prediction_request(...); self.dispatch.predict_with_fallback(query, cluster, request).await
pub use xai_candidate_pipeline::component_library::egress::{EgressConfig, PredictionDispatch, PredictionPath, RetrievalDispatch, RetrievalPath, ...}

runtime_caveats: PredictionDispatch and its predict_with_fallback method are DECLARED/CALLED in checked-in home-mixer source but DEFINED in the external xai_candidate_pipeline::component_library::egress module, which is not part of this published snapshot -- so the actual network dispatch, retry/fallback behavior, and any server-side handling of the request are not independently verifiable from source (see home-mixer/util/egress.rs:L1-L2 for the re-export boundary).

The InputBuffer::new_with_candidates / compute_for_item evidence in phoenix/crates/common/xai-recsys/src/util.rs shows the field being EXTRACTED into per-candidate and per-history-entry feature arrays -- this is STRONG_INFERENCE that it is wired as a model input feature, but it is NOT DIRECT proof that the trained model's learned weights give this feature any material influence on output predictions; that determination requires model-architecture/weight analysis reserved for S05/S06.

S00 did not verify whether this code path executes in the same request as the documented ranking_scorer.rs reply/dwell weight boost, or under what conditions EnableAllAuthorFollowHydration's true default is itself exercised.
notes: This is an example of 'source reveals an undocumented behavioral component' (S00 findings criteria, section 19). The evidence chain BidirectionalFollowHydrator -> PostCandidate.author_follows_viewer -> CandidateHelpers::as_tweet_info -> xai_recsys_proto::AuthorInfo.is_following_user -> build_tweet_infos/build_prediction_request -> PredictNextActionsRequest -> PhoenixScorer::score -> PredictionDispatch::predict_with_fallback is now fully cited hop-by-hop in verification_evidence above. The DIRECT conclusion is bounded precisely at 'the signal is placed into the candidate TweetInfo included in the Phoenix prediction request and that request is sent through PhoenixScorer's prediction dispatch' -- it does not extend to a DIRECT claim that the trained model materially uses the field to alter predictions, which remains an S05/S06 obligation. Should be a priority item for S05's Phoenix feature-provenance review, since a follow-relationship feature feeding the model directly is a materially different mechanism from a fixed post-hoc weight boost and was not flagged anywhere in the two S00-assigned documents that discuss this exact feature area.

title: BidirectionalFollowHydrator's failure behavior on social-graph client error is not fully traceable within S00 scope
claim: When socialgraph_client.check_followed_by errors, BidirectionalFollowHydrator::hydrate returns Err(e.to_string()) for every candidate in the batch. What the candidate-pipeline framework does with a per-candidate hydration Err (drop the candidate, use a default value, fail the whole pipeline stage, retry) is defined by the Hydrator trait/execution engine in candidate-pipeline/, not in this file.
runtime_caveats: Fail-open vs fail-closed behavior for this hydrator's errors is unresolved by S00 and requires reading candidate-pipeline/hydrator.rs's execution engine, which is out of S00's assigned scope.
notes: Lens L04 (failure/fallback behavior) obligation recorded for S01.

title: GrowthBook is a real, wired external runtime-configuration dependency, but only directly evidenced in abuse-enforcement-service, not home-mixer
claim: abuse-enforcement-service/service-lib/src/growthbook.rs and growthbook_writer.rs implement a full GrowthBookClient integration (read config, write config, admin API with a protected endpoint) used by that service. home-mixer/params/param.rs instead binds its param!() defaults to the xai_feature_switches crate, a different runtime-override mechanism. The README's general 'configuration system' language (Experiments and Configuration section) does not name either mechanism explicitly.
runtime_caveats: S00 did not exhaustively search every component for its own runtime-config mechanism; only home-mixer and abuse-enforcement-service were checked directly. Other components (e.g. Phoenix serving, visibility-filtering) may use yet other mechanisms not catalogued here.
missing_dependencies: The external GrowthBook service itself (its URL, keys, and the actual config values it serves) is not part of this repository and cannot be reconstructed from source.
notes: Directly substantiates the architecture map's D17/'GrowthBook' cross-cutting note and is important evidence for the 'Public Snapshot vs Production Reality' section: at least one safety-critical component's runtime behavior is provably controlled by an external, unpublished config service that this repository can write to as well as read from.

title: phoenix/NOTICE documents third-party BSD-3-Clause and Apache-2.0 code bundled inside phoenix/xrex, qualifying a blanket 'whole repo is Apache-2.0' reading
claim: phoenix/NOTICE lists numerous files under phoenix/xrex/cutedsl/ranker_fa4/ and phoenix/xrex/pallas/ as derived from flash-attention and NVIDIA CUTLASS (BSD-3-Clause) and jax-triton (Apache-2.0), each retaining its own original license notice in-file per the NOTICE file's own description.

Only phoenix/ was found to carry a NOTICE file; no other component-level LICENSE/NOTICE files exist in the snapshot.

title: Agatha's cron= definitions are unrelated batch jobs; a distinct config-mirroring marker exists on param.rs and two abuse-enforcement-service rule files, but no artifact implementing that specific sync was found
claim: README.md states: 'we run cron scripts that set the defaults in this repository's code to be the primary production values.' A corrected, broadened repository-wide search found two materially distinct categories of evidence, which must not be conflated: (1) Five literal cron="0 * * * *" definitions exist in agatha/scalding/{data,labels/nsfw,labels/rate_based_labels,labels/spam_suspended,quantile}/BUILD.bazel, each an hourly scalding_job Bazel target owned by agatha-owners@twitter.com depending on Agatha's own offline batch feature/label-extraction jobs -- these are unrelated on their face to home-mixer parameter syncing and do not corroborate the README's claim. (2) Separately, home-mixer/params/param.rs:L1 carries the self-reported header comment '// mirrored from config feature-switch defaults; last sync 2026-08-12T04:09:22Z', and abuse-enforcement-service/service-lib/rules/enforcement_post.yaml:L1 and enforcement_user.yaml:L1 carry the analogous headers '# mirrored from GrowthBook dynamic config; last sync 2026-08-06T16:20:00Z' and '...last sync 2026-08-12T16:22:21Z' respectively. These three files are the only 'mirrored from ...; last sync <timestamp>' artifacts found repository-wide. No cron definition, script, workflow file, or job implementation that PERFORMS this specific header-generating mirroring was found anywhere in the snapshot -- the headers are self-reported metadata stamped onto the target files, not the sync mechanism's own source code.

runtime_caveats: The 'mirrored from ...; last sync ...' headers are self-reported comments on the target files; they are evidence that some process asserts having synced these files, but the process's own implementation (script, job, trigger mechanism) is not published, so it cannot be independently confirmed to be cron-based, on-demand, or otherwise.

The header on param.rs says 'mirrored from config feature-switch defaults', not literally 'primary production values' as README's prose frames it; whether these are the same underlying values is plausible given the matching xai_feature_switches mechanism (S00-F009) but is an interpretive gap, not a proven equivalence.

Absence of a cron/script artifact for this specific mechanism is expected if the sync tooling itself runs in unpublished internal infrastructure, consistent with the README's own 'What's not in this repo?' framing; this finding does not claim the mechanism doesn't exist or isn't cron-triggered, only that neither is established from the published snapshot.
missing_dependencies: The script/job/workflow that produces the 'mirrored from ...; last sync ...' headers is not published in this snapshot.
notes: CORRECTED after independent audit: the original S00 finding stated a repository-wide search for 'cron' returned only the README sentence itself, which was false -- five unrelated Agatha BUILD.bazel scalding_job cron definitions exist and were missed by an insufficiently broad initial search. A corrected, multi-term search (cron, scheduled, schedule, sync, synchronize, generated, param.rs, feature_switch, xai_feature_switches, production values, defaults, config, configuration) was re-run and additionally surfaced the 'mirrored from ...; last sync ...' header convention on param.rs and two abuse-enforcement-service rule YAML files, which is materially stronger evidence of a real config-to-source synchronization mechanism than 'no artifact' -- though it still stops short of proving the mechanism is cron-based or that the synced values are exactly 'the primary production values' as README frames them. See split claims S00-C057 (sync-marker existence, CONFIRMED/DIRECT), S00-C058 (cron specifically, UNKNOWN), and S00-C059 (production-values equivalence, UNKNOWN/POSSIBLE) in S00_claim_matrix.csv. This remains the central evidentiary item bounding how much trust any 'checked-in default = production value' statement in this repository deserves; other findings that treat a checked-in default as production-representative (e.g. S00-F004) should be read against this corrected, more nuanced picture rather than the prior 'no artifact' framing.
